top_choice_rationale: P002 rewards a quantitative flat-band prediction (Bistritzer-MacDonald) and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle graphene (Jarillo-Herrero), with a three-name allocation and a citation that makes no claim about the pairing mechanism. The result is reproduced in many laboratories and opens a new regime of tunable correlated matter. I accept the real timing risk (about eight years old, unresolved mechanism) and the omission of Cao and other early experimentalists, and I rank P001 second because lattice clocks are mature, independently reproduced and cleanly credited to Katori and Ye, even though novelty relative to the 2005 and 2012 prizes is a margin I weigh somewhat lower. Both are preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my electronic-structure and two-dimensional-materials research is close in subject to P002 but I have no documented personal, collaborative or institutional link to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer, Katori or Ye
